stories.notes: Complex cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Openspec needed first to elaborate AC and add technical depth for real-time content rendering and CMS integration. Speckit then hardens with testability, security checks for untrusted content rendering, and edge cases around preview state synchronization.

agentContributions.notes: ACs were empty while description promised concrete functionality (real-time draft previews across GO/UP/MX). Derived measurable ACs and VCs from the description. This is a novel capability — no live-preview path exists in the codebase. All Contentstack components route through useContent → getContentByKey, so that hook and the contentstack service are the attachment points. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs state the mock assumption explicitly and verify what our code renders given known responses.

Openspec provided empty ACs, so all criteria are derived from the story title and description. The original story description is extremely thin ('[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS'), which limits precision — criteria are based on standard expectations for a CMS live-preview feature. I could not inspect the codebase (no tool access), so ACs are written generically. If the codebase already has a useContent hook or Contentstack service, AC-5 and AC-7 should be verified against those actual integration points. AC-6 (authorization) and AC-11 (stale preview URL handling) are security/edge-case additions that are commonly overlooked. AC-8 covers accessibility. AC-10 addresses concurrent editing, a real-world concern for live preview.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added complementary value: openspec identified concrete codebase attachment points (useContent hook, getContentByKey, Contentstack service) and stated mock assumptions for testing, while speckit contributed non-overlapping security and edge-case ACs (authorization AC-6, stale preview URL AC-11, accessibility AC-8, concurrent editing AC-10). However, critical concerns remain: (1) Source ACs were empty and both agents derived all criteria from a one-line title, limiting precision. (2) Speckit explicitly states it had no tool access to inspect the codebase, so its ACs are self-admittedly 'generic' and based on 'standard expectations' rather than actual architecture. (3) acceptanceChanged is false for both agents despite ACs being empty and both claiming to derive criteria — this is contradictory and suggests the derived ACs may not have been written back to the story record. (4) No story split was proposed despite this being a complex cross-platform feature spanning GO, UP, and MX — a single story unit is likely too large. (5) Openspec's claim that 'all Contentstack components route through useContent → getContentByKey' is unverified by speckit. Human review needed to validate codebase assumptions, confirm ACs were actually persisted, and evaluate whether this story should be split.
